Recommendation : It is recommended that the City Council:
(1)
Find that the designation of a historic resource is categorically
exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to
Section 15308 Class 8 of the CEQA Guidelines pertaining to Actions by
Regulatory Agencies for Protection of the Environment and there are no
features that distinguish this project from others in the exempt class and,
therefore, there are no unusual circumstances;
(2)
Find that Doane and Pinney Houses at 840-842 North Fair Oaks Avenue
meet landmark designation criterion C in Pasadena Municipal Code (P.M.C.)
Section 17.62.040(C)(2)(c) because they embody the distinctive
characteristics of historic resource property types, periods and
architectural styles and the Pinney House represents the work of an
architect whose work is significant to the City. The Doane House is an
example of a Queen Anne style single-family residence and the Pinney House
is an example of a Mission Revival Arts & Crafts Period single-family
residence designed by Charles W. Buchanan;
(3)
Adopt a resolution approving a Declaration of Landmark Designation
for 840-842 N. Fair Oaks Avenue, Pasadena, California;
(4)
Authorize the Mayor to execute the Declaration of Landmark
Designation for 840-842 N. Fair Oaks Avenue, Pasadena, California; and
(5)
Direct the City Clerk to record the declaration with the Los Angeles
County Recorder.

December 1, 2020, the Historic Preservation Commission recommended that the

CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  April 26, 2021 - 4:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

PUBLIC HEARING  CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING: PROPOSED ZONING CODE
  AMENDMENTS TO THE CITY'S CANNABIS REGULATIONS -
  PUBLIC HEARING IS CANCELLED AND WILL NOT BE
  DISCUSSED

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, reported that following discussion
  with Councilmember Kennedy and hearing his concerns related to
  the proposed Zoning Code Amendments, and noting that this
  matter was brought forward by staff at his request, and after
  consulting with the City Clerk and City Attorney, that as the
  applicant he has decided to withdraw the application and not move
  forward with the Public Hearing. He noted that the City Council can
  agendize the matter at a future City Council meeting; and
  responded to questions.

  Mayor Gordo requested that Economic Development and
  Technology Committee (EDTech) review the City's cannabis
  regulations, including lessons learned, best practices in other
  communities, and social equity, and provide an update to the City
  Council.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, reported that two letters expressing
  concerns related to the City Clerk and the cancellation of the public
  hearing were received, distributed to the City Council, posted on-
  line, and made part of the public record .

Council Minutes  6  04/26/2021
   Councilmember Hampton expressed concerns with staff's decision
  to cancel the public hearing as the City Council voted to reschedule
  the public hearing and believes that the City Council should be the
  authority to cancel the hearing.

  Michele Beal Bagneris, City Attorney, stated that City Manager
  Mermell initiated the Zoning Code Amendment application, and
  once an application is withdrawn the public hearing is cancelled,
  there is no hearing for the City Council to consider; and responded
  to questions.

  Mayor Gordo stated that he will confer with the City Attorney on the
  process, procedures and authority related to amending or removing
  items on the City Council agenda to provide better clarity on the
  cancellation of public hearings.

  Councilmember Madison expressed disappointment with the
  cancellation process of the public hearing.

  Councilmember Williams asked staff to provide information on the
  revenue impacts of the current operating cannabis operators in the
  City when this item is discussed at a future EDTech meeting.

  Councilmember Kennedy requested that a redacted copy (in terms
  of any sensitive information not for public display) of his letter
  expressing his concerns on the matter be forwarded to staff and the
  Chair of the Economic Development Technology Committee.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the discussion regarding the proposed Zoning
  Code Amendments related to the City's cannabis regulations was
  forwarded to the Economic Development and Technology
  Committee for further consideration and discussion.

REPORTS AND  APPROVAL OF BUDGET AMENDMENT AND LOAN
COMMENTS FROM  AGREEMENTS FOR FIVE (5) PROJECTS UNDER THE SECOND
COUNCIL COMMITTEES  UNIT ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT LOAN PILOT PROGRAM
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:

Council Minutes  12  04/26/2021
   (1) Find that the proposed actions are exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") in accordance with State
  CEQA Guidelines Sections 15301 (existing facilities), and there are
  no features that distinguish the project from others in the exempt
  class and, therefore, there are no unusual circumstances;
  (2) Approve a budget amendment appropriating $674,500 from
  the lnclusionary Housing Trust Fund's unappropriated fund balance
  to the Housing Department's Fiscal Year (FY) 2021 Operating
  Budget to be used for loan funding ($600,000) and third-party
  project management contract services ($74,500); (Budget
  Amendment No. 2021-34)
  (3) Approve the five (5) loan agreements totaling $600,000 for
  accessory dwelling unit projects under the Second Unit Accessory
  Dwelling Unit Pilot Program (the "Program") as described in the
  agenda report; and
  (4) Authorize the City Manager to execute, and the City Clerk to
  attest, the loan agreements, and any and all documents to
  effectuate the Program. (Contract Nos. E. Holle 32014; J. Hayden
  32018; M. Bugarin 32019; C. Lopez 32020; H. Menakian and R.
  Blakeley 32021)
  Councilmember Hampton, Chair of the Economic Development and
  Technology Committee, summarized the discussion at the
  Committee meeting, including Councilmember Madison's concerns
  related to the staff recommendation.

  William Huang, Director of Housing, provided introductory
  comments, and Randy Mabson, Program Coordinator, presented a
  PowerPoint presentation on the item , and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with the City's
  Accessary Dwelling Unit (ADU) Loan Pilot Program selected
  participants, which are located in only three of the City's Council
  Districts, stating that he believes the dwellings should be dispersed
  throughout the City. He also expressed concerns with the
  perception that the City might be seen as "rewarding" unpermitted
  construction activity by providing loans to rehabilitate unpermitted
  ADU's.

  Councilmember Hampton spoke in favor of the staff
  recommendation, which he believes will help homeowners build
  ADU's to provide affordable housing for family members.

  Mayor Gordo spoke in favor of the staff recommendation, and
  asked staff to monitor the pilot program and note any "lessons
